subject: Privacy & retention options — post-demo recap and next steps
messages:
From: Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv.kapoor@neurowave.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@neuroprocure.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T16:12:00+00:00
Subject: Thanks — quick privacy/retention clarifications

Michael — thanks for the call earlier. Short recap from our side and a couple of clarifying asks before we loop procurement: 

- Goal: run a 4-week POC that processes clinician notes and triage chat. Data contains PHI/PII.
- Primary ask: Can Redwood support a configuration where model inputs and outputs are not persisted (0-retention) for our POC? We understand some telemetry/metrics may be required for billing/operational support — we need to keep that minimal.
- Secondary ask: If true 0-retention isn’t possible on Hosted, what are your shortest supported retention windows (e.g., 24h, 72h, 7d)? Also curious about whether KV caching can be kept strictly in-memory and never written to disk.
- Residency: EU region required (data must remain in eu-west-1 region).

Also attaching the procurement template — Priya from NeuroProcure will handle contracts. Please confirm what evidence (SOC 2, encryption, KMS options) we can provide this week so procurement can advance.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Head of Platform
NeuroWave Health

[attachment: procurement_template.docx (docx)]

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv.kapoor@neurowave.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@neuroprocure.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T17:05:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick privacy/retention clarifications

Rajiv — really appreciate the clear list. Summary and a few concrete options below so procurement has something to review. I’m attaching a DPA redline and a short tech note on our ephemeral mode.

Options for the POC (pros/cons):

1) True ephemeral (recommended for PHI POC)
   - Inputs/outputs never persisted to long-term storage; KV cache kept in-memory on GPU nodes and flushed on session end.
   - Minimal operational telemetry retained: request id, timestamps, token counts for billing (we can truncate identifiers).
   - Requires either Dedicated or Private deployment for strict isolation; Hosted can be configured for near-ephemeral but may leave short-term traces in our logging backend.

2) Short-window logs (hosted friendly)
   - Retention window configurable: 24h / 72h / 7d. Logs are encrypted at rest and stored in EU region.
   - Useful if your team needs short-term replay for debugging. We can redact PII fields before persistence as part of the pipeline.

3) Hybrid: 0-retain for content, 30d aggregated telemetry for performance (no raw inputs).
   - Gives procurement a middle ground for auditability without storing PII.

Evidence we can provide this week:
- SOC 2 Type II summary + scope notes (EU region ops)
- KMS options: customer-managed keys via supported cloud KMS or our managed keys (we can enable CMK for private deployments)
- Architecture note describing ephemeral mode + KV eviction (attached).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll loop in engineering and legal to confirm feasibility and the likely topology for a POC.
- If you’re good with option 1 or 3, we can schedule a technical scoping call (30–45m) with Aditya (runtime) and Laura (security) this week.
- I’ll send a redlined DPA for Priya to review.

Would you prefer a dedicated temporary cluster for the POC (recommended) or hosted with strict retention and redaction?

Best,

Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0126

Attachments:
- redwood_dpa_redline.pdf
- ephemeral-mode-tech-note.md

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-11T17:12:00+00:00
Subject: Fwd: Thanks — quick privacy/retention clarifications — POC asks (need feasibility & config)

Forwarding Rajiv’s note and my reply — short asks from procurement re: 0-retention and EU residency. Can you confirm feasibility for the POC and cost delta for a temporary dedicated cluster?

Key questions: 
- Can we guarantee no persistent copies of inputs/outputs on Hosted if we enable ephemeral runtime and in-memory KV only? If not, what is the minimal retention and where would traces live?
- Can we enable CMK (customer-managed keys) for a short-lived Dedicated cluster tied to NeuroWave’s KMS?
- Any red flag re: SOC2 scope or audit evidence that we should proactively send?

Aditya — can you sketch an ops checklist for a 4-week POC (networking, encryption, eviction behavior, retention window config)? Laura — from a security/legal standpoint, anything we must call out before sending the DPA redline to procurement? Monica — procurement hooks/pricing lead here.

Thanks — MG

Date: 2027-04-12T08:40:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Thanks — quick privacy/retention clarifications — POC asks (need feasibility & config)

Short answers from runtime/ops POV: 

- Ephemeral mode: yes — for Dedicated and Private we can run the POC with volatile-only storage. Inputs/outputs stay in RAM/GPU memory; KV cache can be kept in-memory and never checkpointed. We would still emit minimal operational telemetry (request_id, duration, tokens) to an encrypted, access-restricted metrics store for billing and health. We can make those metrics stripped of identifiers.
- Hosted constraints: on our multi-tenant Hosted we cannot promise absolute zero traces in internal ephemeral caches for every component. For strict 0-retention we should use Dedicated or Private.
- CMK: supported on Dedicated (AWS KMS customer-managed keys). We can schedule key rotation aligned with the 4-week POC.
- Cost/property delta: temporary Dedicated cluster (2 x a40-equivalent) for 4 weeks — estimate +35% over a comparable hosted run due to reserved instance overhead and isolation. Exact quote from Monica.

Ops checklist (high level):
- Provision dedicated cluster in eu-west-1 with CMK attached
- Configure runtime in ephemeral mode, KV eviction on session end
- Disable persistent logs; enable truncated telemetry (no raw text)
- Run integration tests for redaction pipeline before PV is accepted

I’ll draft a short ops runbook and send it to Michael and Laura by EOD.

— Aditya

From: Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv.kapoor@neurowave.ai>

Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@neuroprocure.com>, legal@neurowave.ai
Date: 2027-04-14T09:20:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick privacy/retention clarifications

Thanks for the quick internal checks — that helps. A couple of clarifications and requests before procurement signs off: 

1) We strongly prefer option 1 (True ephemeral) for the POC. What you described sounds acceptable provided you can:
   - Guarantee no persistent storage of inputs/outputs for the duration of the POC
   - Provide the ops runbook and evidence of CMK attachment to the Dedicated cluster

2) Telemetry: we accept stripped metrics (request id + token counts) but need those to be retained no more than 30 days and never include user identifiers.

3) Evidence: please attach SOC2 summary and a short note on encryption key handling. If you can provide a brief example of the runtime eviction log (format) that would be very helpful for our auditors.

4) Timeline: procurement would like a contract-ready DPA this week and a technical scoping call with Aditya & team on Mon 04/19 10:00 CEST (works for your folks?).

If you can confirm the above and send the updated DPA, we’ll route to Priya + legal and aim to sign the POC agreement next week.

Best,
Rajiv
